grandparents_cupboard.reason: Flour, butter, cheddar, eggs, milk, pears and thyme are all plain home staples with no factory-made products.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream supermarket at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, grater, knife and baking tray, and rubbing in and patting out a scone round is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: The flour, butter and liquid are in sensible proportions with the pears adding moisture, a hot oven for 15 to 18 minutes suits scone wedges, and 8 wedges is right for a snack for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers rubbing in, dicing two pears, grating the cheese and shaping, and the 18-minute cook matches the bake time in the method.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including salt and the fresh thyme, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm pear and cheddar scones suit an early November afternoon, and the pears are a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow without any restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Part-wholemeal scones with fruit, cheese and egg make a satisfying real-food snack that a family would happily bake again.
